reviews.title: Best CPU AIO for under $100, hands down.
reviews.comment: I've bought 10+ ID Cooler AIO's for build for people and absolutely love them. The waterblock is the center of most builds and having one without obnoxious branding, RGB only fit to light a basement or a stupid little screen is such a breath if fresh air. The price is amazing, I usually use the extra $$$ left over to upgrade the fans. The cooling performance has been rock solid. No issues on multiple Ryzen 9's I've installed them on over the years, all are still running strong and quiet. Install is easy as can be.
reviews.author: Marley

reviews.title: Solid budget AIO
reviews.comment: Much cooler temps than I expected. Works as intended. Wanted to pair this with my new motherboard/ setup. Kept my i7-13700 at a low 33c and gaming at 1440p was around 65c to 66c. Not bad. My system is a lot more quiet now.
reviews.author: Jpo Fett

reviews.title: The Iceman cometh
reviews.comment: Overheating is a thing if the past.  This gizmo is awesome.  Easy install.  Not meant for my case so measure and plan accordingly.  After some creative 'readjustments' got everything up and running.  Highly recommend

reviews.title: Ice cold 🧊
reviews.comment: Keeps my cpu nice & cool, packaged very well. Pump has a clean pure matte/flat white aesthetics. 4 pin pwm fans are preinstalled & linked together, extension is included too.
reviews.author: Giovanni Tovar

reviews.title: Perfect for my wife's AM5 build
reviews.comment: I'm working on an all-white AM5 build for my wife. While I have a 420mm AIO on my build, hers will be a more pedestrian build. I wanted something that could keep the chip nice and cool, while also being quiet and pretty. This ID-Cooling fit the bill perfectly. Setup and installation was extremely straightforward. The 2x 120mm PWM fans move a decent amount of air and are quiet for this price. The pump does make some noise on startup as it ramps up - but then it quiets down to a more reasonable level. I have the pump running around 80% and the fans at a lower speed. Her CPU is staying nice and cool, even under load. While I don't intend on moving her PC around much, I like that the case itself is carrying the burden of the weight. My only recommendation would be to ensure that you have adequate cooling around your VRMs. While some liquid coolers put a small fan on the block to keep air moving around your VRMs, this does not. This isn't a dealbreaker, simply ensure that you have some good air flow with your case fans to keep air moving around the VRMs. Overall, I'm very impressed with this entry-level liquid cooler.
reviews.author: Ron B
